_: The world's components and the models that draw them, one place (realistic.gd reads it through data.gd; docs/TUNING.md). A placer asks for a component (fence, house_poor, keep...), never a file, so a new art family is an edit here. Shape: Paradox's entity files and RimWorld's ThingDef graphicData. Per component: kind (what the town rules ask for: house, hall, barn, prop, clutter...) and variants. Per variant: model (under res://assets; a folder means its scene.gltf), name (the name placers used before the catalogue, kept while they move over), length (its true longest side in metres: the scale), height (its true height in metres, used for the scale instead when the length misleads: a tall stack, a lying cluster), and optionally strip (parts the land supplies itself), floorCut (game units: triangles under it dropped), stone (no glow), dye (materials by name, each colour multiplied by [r, g, b] and renamed Dyed_<name> so team colour leaves it: a market stall's awning; or {"paint": [r, g, b]}, the cloth repainted in that colour with its weave kept: the yard washing's linen), weight (how often it's picked). Order matters: it is the order placers pick in. heightRange: the true height a component should stand, in metres (lowest, highest): tools/scale_check.gd fails a model outside it (a hut must never stand as tall as a castle tower). switch and kit: a component whose switch (castles, houses: realm/data/towns.json, or --castles=kit / --houses=kit) is kit draws from its kit list instead: variants our builders raise from the Quaternius Medieval Village kit (builder house: house_builder.gd, spec w and d in 2 m cells, floors, style plaster|timber|brick, seed, chimney (the chance of one, 0.7 unset); builder castle: castle_builder.gd, spec w, d bailey cells, wall_storeys, keep cells, keep_storeys, tower_storeys, side_towers, banner, seed), built in metres. The castle list is by rank: the crown's seat takes the first, a great house's the last.

woods._: Which trees the woods grow (forest.gd). set: pack (the realistic pine, oak and bush packs) or kit (Quaternius Stylized Nature, the painted look); --trees=pack or --trees=kit overrides. kit: per role (pine, oak, bush) the model files and the true height in metres a grown one stands; young and sapling: how tall the younger trees are, as a share of grown. Grown trees stand one to two houses tall (a kit cottage about 6 m, a townhouse about 9 m: tools/scale_check.gd holds the grown heights to tree_range, metres); they were 17 and 15 m and read huge beside the houses from mid zoom (Warcraft III: clustered stylised trees at a house and a half). pack_scale: the realistic packs come at their true size (13-31 m); this share of it.

kit._leaves: leaf_texture: a kit leaf material's texture swapped by name (the twisted tree's leaves are painted solid red and read as red blobs; they take the common tree's green and turn with the season). seasons: by model file, the tint over its summer colour each season (forest.gd _leaves, terrain.gd's season pass), so a wood turns as a mix (art target 01-town: mostly deep green, some ochre, amber and rust; two of the seven broadleaf kinds turn amber or rust, one ochre-green, the rest stay green: from mid zoom the woods read green with warm accents, not red and orange dots); a model not listed takes the land's season tint.

house_kit._: How house_tiers.gd composes a kit house of each tier from the Medieval Village kit (house_builder.gd bakes it; docs/TUNING.md). scale: the size a tiered kit house stands at, a share of the kit's metres (scale_kinds: the components it applies to; scale_tiers: the trades' tiers that stand at it too, one storey height round the square, their work spots scaled with them; mills keep the kit's, their sails and wheels hang in its metres): the kit's 3 m storeys and steep roofs stood a two-storey townhouse 9.7 m to the ridge and a merchant's 12-15 m beside 1.7 m townsfolk; at 0.85 a storey is 2.55 m, a townhouse 8.0-8.7 m to the ridge (research: a two-storey house 7-9 m), a three-storey merchant's or burgher's about 11.5. washes: the plaster's limewash colours (cream, white, ochre, rose, grey-blue, daub), a tint over the kit's plaster (above 1: the kit's plaster photo is a dull beige, so a warm cream wash lifts it; art target town-b: warm cream, ochre and rose plaster). stone_tint and timber_tint: the kit's stone (MI_UnevenBrick) and timber (MI_WoodTrim) on every kit house, lifted to honey stone and honey timber (they read near black under the grade). roof_weather: per house (by its seed) one of these multiplied over its roof covering's tint, new to dark weathered tile (house_tiers.gd _roof_look). stone_tint_v3: the tiered houses' stone under the v3 look, grey as 01-town's and the castle's (stone_tint, honey, otherwise); timber_tint_v3 their timber under v3, dark against white plaster (timber_tint otherwise). roof_uv: how many times more often the tile sheet repeats on a tiered roof (finer tiles; 1 the kit's). Round 3 (roofs huge, walls hidden): pitch lowered (tile 0.78, thatch 1.0, were 0.9, 1.12) and the square's tiers half-timbered more (townhouse, merchant, burgher timber 0.65, 0.6, 0.5). roof_tints: each roof covering's tint when team colour is off (team colour on draws thatch as straw and slate and shingle in these tones; look.json team.roofs). pitch: how steep each covering stands (a share of the kit's own pitch; thatch steepest). banner_scale: the holder's wall banner on a house's street front (extras.banner, Banner_1 is 1.6 x 2.4 m at 1). jetty_m: how far each upper storey of a jettied house leans out over the street (metres). Finesse (Mac 2026-11-12, 'no finesse'): window_glow, the kit's window glass as warm lit amber (colour, alpha, emission energy; house_builder.gd _glass); 01-town pass: the square's tiers thatched about 1 in 3, half-timbered over plaster (plain plaster 0.05), jettied more (townhouse 0.8, merchant 0.75, burgher 0.5); extras.door_lamp, a lantern on its post beside the front door (door_lamp: its file and height in metres; Kenney's town lantern, CC0); extras.door_frame, the kit's door frame round the front door (dark timber, stone on a stone front); shutters on most of the square's windows; a hanging sign on the forge, the armoury and the granary. tiers: per tier, ranges [lowest, highest] or numbers: w and d (2 m cells across the front and deep), floors, ridge (along: gable to the street, Manor Lords' burgage; across: eaves to the street with dormers, Anno's merchants), roofs and walls (weights: stone, stone_timber, timber, plaster), washes (which wash colours it may take), jetty (chance), dormers (per slope), dormers_back, chimney (chance of a stone stack up a gable), ridge_chimneys, pitch (on top of the covering's), round_windows (share), windows (share of wall panels with a window: front_ground, front, back, sides; party walls are mostly blind), shutters, shop (wide shop windows either side of the door), arcade (the ground floor's front open in arches), extras (chances; banner: the holder's banner down the upper street front; porch, sign, lean_to, outside_stair, balcony, window_boxes, vines), props (baked in: [piece, [x, y, z] metres, yaw, scale, anchor front|back|centre]; a bare name is the village kit's, res:// any glTF).

_poses: A skinned figure stood still as plain meshes (realistic.gd still): its path -> [clip, seconds into it]. The crown's square's king (square_statue) stands as a monument, sword in hand (Idle_Sword; was his idle): carved in warm stone with a burnished gilt crown and trim and a red cloak, on a tall dressed-stone plinth of warm stone, moulded top and base, three steps, flowers round it (Mac 2026-11-12: 'no finesse', a live-coloured figure on a lumpy rock; 01-town's monument; round 8: too small, a white figure lost in the square, so life and a half and more, about 3.7 m, on a 2.4 m plinth, 7.5 m in all).

components._tiers: House tiers and the town's working buildings (house_tiers.gd composes each from the kit by its tier in house_kit.tiers; towns.json tiers and trades place them). count: that many models of the tier, each its own seed. trade: the trade it houses for the life at it (works.gd, data/works.json); work_front: its work spots, [across, out] or [across, out, up] in metres, out measured from its front wall's line (negative is inside), turned and placed into the town's works meta by towns.gd; a spot named hearth glows; smoke: its chimney smokes. walled: a low wall round its ground with a gate before its door ({pad: metres, wall: its component, garden: beds inside}: the churchyard, the manor's walled garden). rotor: a mill's turning part as its own node (works.gd turns it by name, about works.json mill.axis): model, name (sail, wheel), axis it turns on in the building's frame (z out of its front, x along it), from (front or back: the wall it stands off; a watermill's wheel is on its back, in the water), out and up (metres from that wall's foot), across (metres from its middle), size (its true diameter). switch trade_art (realm/data/towns.json): kit (raised from the kit, or the catalogue model) or ai (image-to-3D models, the ai list; --trade_art=ai).
components._roadside: Life along the roads (roadside.gd, realm/data/roadside.json): kit stand-ins until image-to-3D models land (roadside.json candidates). Kind roadside: buildings; roadprop: small things.
components._files: Components below are files their own placer loads and sizes (no length: not kit models): the woods, the crops, war gear.
